definitions.gloss: renting a room (in someone's house); subletting; lodging
definitions.explanation: Renting a room within someone else's home or existing space, rather than renting an entire apartment or house. Can also refer to borrowing part of a commercial space.

examples.japanese: {間借|まが}りで{暮|く}らしている。
examples.english: I'm living in a rented room.

examples.japanese: {知人|ちじん}の{家|いえ}に{間借|まが}りする。
examples.english: To rent a room at an acquaintance's house.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}の{頃|ころ}は{大家|おおや}さんの{家|いえ}の{二階|にかい}を{間借|まが}りしていた。
examples.english: When I was a student, I rented the second floor of the landlord's house.

notes:
Describes renting part of a space, not the whole unit. Traditionally refers to renting a room in someone's home, a common arrangement in older Japan and still seen today. Recently also used for businesses sharing commercial space (e.g., a pop-up restaurant operating inside another restaurant's space).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {間借|まが}りする: to rent a room / to sublet
- {間借|まが}り{人|にん}: lodger / tenant
- {間借|まが}り{生活|せいかつ}: life as a lodger
- {間借|まが}りカレー: pop-up curry restaurant (operating inside another space)
- {間借|まが}り{営業|えいぎょう}: operating out of a shared/borrowed space

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {下宿|げしゅく}: boarding house / lodging — a house specifically set up to take in boarders, with meals often included
- {賃貸|ちんたい}: rental — renting an entire apartment or house
- {同居|どうきょ}: living together — sharing a home, but implies a closer relationship

MODERN USAGE:
The term {間借|まが}り has gained new life in the food industry, where {間借|まが}り{営業|えいぎょう} refers to a restaurant operating inside another establishment's space during off-hours, a popular low-cost way to start a food business.
